$comment: Rule classes from eslint-plugin-security that we deliberately do NOT implement. This is a product position, not a coverage gap — each entry must carry a defensible reason and be safe to state publicly. Excluded from relevance-weighted parity; still reported in raw parity so the number is never quietly inflated.
policy: A rule earns a place only if it detects a defect that can still occur in code written for currently-supported runtimes. Parity with a competitor is not a reason to ship a rule.

detect-pseudoRandomBytes.reason: crypto.pseudoRandomBytes still exists, but it IS crypto.randomBytes: `crypto.pseudoRandomBytes === crypto.randomBytes` is true on every supported Node (24 versions measured, 18.16.1 to 26.10.0, on 2026-10-25). The API is the CSPRNG, so the weak-randomness defect cannot occur. oxlint-plugin-security keeps the ID as a deprecated no-op.
detect-pseudoRandomBytes.reconsiderIf: A supported Node release makes pseudoRandomBytes differ from randomBytes.

detect-no-csrf-before-method-override.reason: The rule matches only express.csrf() and express.methodOverride() — Express 3 built-ins, not csurf. On Express 4.22.3 reading express.csrf throws ("Most middleware (like csrf) is no longer bundled"); on 5.3.0 both are undefined. The defect cannot be written against a supported Express. oxlint-plugin-security keeps the ID as a deprecated no-op.
detect-no-csrf-before-method-override.reconsiderIf: A supported Express major bundles csrf or methodOverride again.

detect-unsafe-regex.reason: We cover ReDoS in valid patterns (`new RegExp('(x+x+)+y')` reports via secure-coding/no-redos-vulnerable-regex). The single open case is `new RegExp('x+x+)+y')` — a SYNTACTICALLY INVALID regex (unmatched paren), which core ESLint's `no-invalid-regexp` already reports with a better message. Duplicating a core rule violates our taxonomy doctrine; an unparseable pattern is a syntax error, not a ReDoS.
detect-unsafe-regex.reconsiderIf: Our ReDoS analyser is found to silently skip patterns that ARE parseable by the JS engine — that would be a genuine blind spot rather than a syntax error.
